new_statements.rule_in_words: Across the Wetar languages surveyed, including Ili'uun (Ilmaumau list), word stress falls on the penultimate syllable; words deviating from this are individually marked in the lists, and for Ili'uun only two items are so marked, both with final stress (api'suŋ 'machete', aci'me 'where').
new_statements.exceptions: Lexical exceptions marked with a pre-syllable apostrophe in the word lists: Ili'uun api'suŋ 'machete', aci'me 'where' (final stress). For closely related Tugun (sec. 6.2 p.115) the aspectual clitics -e/-me shift stress to the root-final syllable; no such morphological detail is given for Ili'uun.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is a transcription convention for elicited citation forms (210-item survey word lists); group-level claim for 'Wetar languages' by the fieldworker who collected the Ili'uun lists, not an Ili'uun-specific phonological analysis. Editor (Grimes) adds that apparent monosyllables are like-vowel sequences and 'Word stress remains penultimate.'
new_statements.identity_note: Hinton's statement is a group-level convention for 'Wetar languages' (Perai, Aputai, Talur, Tugun, Ili'uun) by the fieldworker who elicited the Ili'uun lists; the printed Ili'uun list is from Ilmaumau village (ilma1240, a Glottolog dialect of iliu1237), with lists also taken at Telemar, Karbubu, Ustutun, Klishatu, Eray, Nabar, Esulit. The detailed stress rule (sec. 6.2) is for Tugun (tugu1245), not Ili'uun. The unlocated Penn 2006 describes Dadu'a (dadu1237), the Ili'uun offshoot in Timor-Leste; de Josselin de Jong 1947 describes Erai (eray1237).

sources.note: p.119 (Appendix B, transcription symbols for the five printed word lists incl. Ili'uun of Ilmaumau): 'Stress in Wetar languages is generally penultimate. It is marked with an apostrophe preceding the stressed syllable where different.' Ili'uun forms carrying the exception mark (p.126): api'suŋ 'machete', aci'me 'where'. Editor's note p.119: 'Word stress remains penultimate.' Sec. 6.2 p.115 gives the Tugun-specific rule (penultimate; clitics -e/-me shift stress to root-final).
